headline: High-risk default interaction: Devin’s autonomous write/network/tool access can amplify any content from the non-runnable awesome-nlp list into unsafe actions or leaks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Devin’s outputs. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or external reuse of list content into Devin’s autonomous workspace, which is an unusual configuration. Devin’s browser, MCP, and autonomous tool use make it susceptible if attacker-controlled text is introduced, but the pair itself lacks a default shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies awesome-nlp content into Devin’s prompt or workspace, injection becomes plausible.
IF Devin is connected to an MCP server that forwards untrusted text from the list, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp and Devin in separate workflows.
Disable copy/paste of untrusted list content into Devin sessions.
Require a human review step before Devin acts on any imported text.
Use a provenance tag for any content transferred into Devin.
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, so it is not a meaningful source of leakage. Devin, however, reads files and uses broad network egress plus third-party integrations, so if sensitive material is placed into its workspace it can leave the environment. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so the blast radius is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive files are copied into Devin’s cloud workspace, they may be transmitted through its integrations.
IF the operator treats awesome-nlp content as a source of secrets, leakage risk remains low because the list itself stores none.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in Devin’s workspace.
Restrict Devin integrations to the minimum required services.
Review outbound artifacts before sharing them externally.
Separate documentation browsing from secret-bearing repos.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Devin integrations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or execution capabilities, while Devin can write files, modify git state, and run shells in a shared cloud workspace. There is no direct conflict between the two agents, but if awesome-nlp content is used to steer Devin’s edits, Devin’s broad write surface can create collisions with repository state or other collaborators. Uncertainty about any orchestrator locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin is pointed at a repository already being edited by another actor, git/file conflicts can occur.
IF awesome-nlp-derived instructions cause Devin to rewrite shared files, capability overlap becomes operationally relevant.
mitigations: Assign Devin a dedicated branch or workspace.
Pause parallel edits while Devin runs.
Require git status checks before each write.
Limit Devin to read-only mode for review tasks.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking across agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a static list, but Devin’s autonomous planner-executor model can treat imported text as actionable guidance. If the list is used as a source of recommendations, Devin may execute or commit changes without a strong verification step. The pathway is not guaranteed, yet Devin’s default autonomy makes downstream mistakes plausible even though awesome-nlp itself does not act.
conditions: IF Devin uses awesome-nlp entries as authoritative recommendations, it may propagate errors into code or tickets.
IF no human verification step is inserted before Devin acts, cascading mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin executes recommendations.
Cross-check imported claims against primary sources.
Limit Devin to drafting, not applying, changes.
Annotate list-derived suggestions as unverified.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is identified in either profile, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch to score higher. Devin does handle source code, docs, and integrations with retention-sensitive systems, but awesome-nlp itself is just an open-source list with no touched data classes. The compliance risk is therefore limited to generic governance gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Devin’s integrations, residency and retention controls must be re-evaluated.
IF the operator uses Devin on data subject to stricter policies than source code/docs, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin unless approved.
Review retention settings on connected integrations.
Document data classes allowed in Devin sessions.
Use separate workspaces for regulated and non-regulated work.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
